name: Majnun Layla
bio: Qays ibn al-Mulawwah, of the tribe of Amir ibn Sa'sa'a, was a love poet of Najd, called the Majnun, “the madman”, for his passion for Layla bint Sa'd. Al-Zirikli says he was not mad, and gives the story told of him: he grew up with Layla until her father kept her from him, then wandered the wilderness reciting poems and keeping company with wild animals, until he was found dead among rocks; he dates his death to 68 AH (688 CE). Whether he lived at all was disputed early, as al-Aghani reports: al-Asma'i called the Majnun and Ibn al-Qirriyya “two men known in the world only by name, whom the transmitters made up”, and Ibn al-Kalbi had heard that a young Umayyad in love with his cousin invented the Majnun's story and poems. The same book reports men who said they had seen him and heard him recite, and his modern editor Abd al-Sattar Farraj holds that most reports confirm he lived, and that much of what was said about Layla came to be credited to him.
